Finance Minister Abul Maal Abdul Muhit. Year October monthly report. Daily taka transactions in mobile banking. Saturday, in the National Parliament, in reply to a question from M Abdul Latif of the ruling party, the finance minister said this, according to a BSS report. Bangladesh Bank efforts to reduce service charges are continuing through multiple meetings with banks and mobile network operators. A huge population living in remote areas has very limited access to conventional banking services, so to bring this huge population under banking services, Bangladesh Bank has approved banks providing mobile banking services following the bank-led model. In continuation of Muhit's initiative, in the mobile banking system banks appoint branch agents and provide the necessary financial service activities. The finance minister said that when considering customer expenditure and agent accessibility and time matters, customers find it convenient, whereas taking existing banking services requires going to the nearby branch, which costs time and money. Mobile banking delivers banking services to customers at comparatively low cost. Efforts continue, and Muhit said that to create a competitive market, Bangladesh Bank is formulating and implementing a mobile banking policy so that services are delivered to people's doorsteps at low cost.
